label: RB4011iGS+5HacQ2HnD-IN
description: MikroTik RB4011iGS+5HacQ2HnD-IN (RB4011iGS+5HacQ2HnD-IN) - 10x 1G RJ45, 1x 10G SFP+, Wi-Fi 2.4/5 GHz. Powered by the DC jack or by passive PoE-in on eth1 only (18-57 V); passive PoE-out on eth10. ARM 32bit 4-core AL21400.
notes: Vendor rows read 2026-11-28 from https://mikrotik.com/product/rb4011igs_5hacq2hnd_in: **Number of DC inputs 2 (DC jack, PoE-IN)**, **PoE in Passive PoE**, **PoE in input Voltage 18-57 V**, **PoE-out ports Ether10**, **PoE out Passive PoE**, **Max power consumption 44 W**, **Max power consumption without attachments 23 W**. Which socket the inlet is, https://manual.mikrotik.com/hardware/rb4011igs-plus-5hacq2hnd-in/ (read 2026-11-28): "The device accepts power from the power jack or from the first Ethernet port: ... First Ethernet port accepts Power over Ethernet 18-57 V DC." So `eth1` is the one inlet and it draws the board's 23 W ceiling; `eth2`-`eth9` declare poeIn: false, and `eth10` is PoE-out only - a PSE port cannot be fed. The row used to spell `eth1` as `poeIn: true`, a shape the schema does not allow as a wattage, and the eight sockets beside it were inheriting the 12.95 W 802.3af guess from `category: wireless` - 103.6 W of demand from a router whose PoE-in is passive 18-57 V.
